harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ 3.13.7 cluster (node1/node2/node3, RHEL 9) using Team RabbitMQ's official Cloudsmith repos for Erlang 26 and rabbitmq-server. Created a dedicated CA on node1 (4096-bit RSA, 10y validity) that issued per-node server certs (SANs for hostname+IP) and one client cert. AMQP is served exclusively over TLS on 5671 (plaintext 5672 disabled via listeners.tcp=none) with verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, so only clients presenting a certificate signed by the cluster CA can connect — verified positively (successful publish/consume with the CA-issued client cert) and negatively (TLS alert 'certificate_required' with no cert, 'unknown_ca' alert with a cert from a different CA). The management HTTP API (15672) is bound only to each node's private cluster IP (not 0.0.0.0) and additionally firewalld-restricted (rich rules) to the 10.100.130.0/24 cluster subnet, with the public zone otherwise deny-by-default — confirmed reachable from a cluster peer (node2→node1 returned HTTP 401, i.e. TCP+HTTP reached the API) while not exposed on any other interface. Cluster formed via rabbitmqctl join_cluster with a shared Erlang cookie; cluster_status confirms all 3 nodes running with no partitions. Completed the mandatory rolling-restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and RabbitMQ/cluster health per node, restarted node2 → node3 → node1 one at a time (each `reboot` acknowledged before disconnect), polled until each came back, and proved a changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id per node. After each restart verified RabbitMQ auto-started, cluster membership and a durable quorum queue (created with a test message before the restarts) remained healthy/online with the message intact throughout, and confirmed TLS+client-cert enforcement and firewall/management restrictions were unaffected after the full cycle. All credentials (Erlang cookie, testadmin password) were generated on-node and never appeared as literals in tool commands (passed via command substitution reading root-only files).
actions_performed: Installed Erlang 26 and RabbitMQ 3.13.7 on node1/node2/node3 via official Cloudsmith repos
Configured /etc/hosts with cluster name mappings and set up passwordless inter-node SSH using CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/PRIVKEY
Built a self-signed CA on node1 and issued per-node TLS server certs (SAN=hostname+IP) and a client cert, distributed CA cert + server cert/key to each node's /etc/rabbitmq/tls
Distributed a shared random Erlang cookie to /var/lib/rabbitmq/.erlang.cookie and /root/.erlang.cookie on all nodes
Wrote rabbitmq.conf on each node: disabled plaintext AMQP, enabled AMQPS on 5671 with verify_peer+fail_if_no_peer_cert, bound management HTTP API to the node's private IP only
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin on all nodes
Configured firewalld: opened 5671/tcp broadly; restricted 15672 (management), 25672 (clustering) and 4369 (epmd) to source 10.100.130.0/24 only via rich rules
Started RabbitMQ on node1, then node2 and node3, joined node2 and node3 to the node1-seeded cluster via rabbitmqctl join_cluster
Verified cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running with no partitions
Created a non-default administrator user (testadmin) with an on-node-generated random password (never placed in a tool command literally)

Verified TLS+client-cert enforcement: AMQPS publish/consume succeeded cross-node with the CA-issued client cert; connection rejected with certificate_required alert when no client cert supplied; connection rejected with unknown_ca alert when a cert from a different self-signed CA was supplied
Verified management API is bound only to each node's private IP (ss -tlnp) and reachable from a cluster peer but not exposed on 0.0.0.0
Created a durable quorum queue with a persisted test message to track data health across restarts

Executed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and health for all 3 nodes, restarted node2, then node3, then node1 one at a time via native `reboot` with backgrounded ack-before-disconnect, polled each node until exec access returned, confirmed changed boot_id per node, and verified RabbitMQ service active, cluster membership restored, and the quorum queue online/healthy with its message intact after each restart
Re-verified TLS client-cert enforcement and firewall/management-binding restrictions were unchanged after the full restart cycle
Cleaned up ephemeral test queues

evidence.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status shows all three nodes as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes, no partitions, both before and after the full restart cycle

evidence.requirement: AMQP served over TLS using a cluster-created CA
evidence.summary: CA generated on node1, per-node server certs issued and verified against it (openssl verify OK), rabbitmq.conf sets listeners.tcp=none and listeners.ssl.default=5671 with ca/cert/keyfile, and ss confirms port 5671 listening

evidence.requirement: Only clients with a CA-issued certificate are accepted
evidence.summary: TLS handshake and AMQP publish/consume succeed with the CA-issued client cert (Verify return code 0, message round-tripped); connections without a client cert fail with TLS alert 'certificate_required' (server log + client SSL error); connections with a cert from a different CA fail with 'unknown_ca'; re-confirmed after all node restarts

evidence.requirement: Management interface reachable only from within the cluster
evidence.summary: management.tcp.ip bound to each node's private cluster IP only (ss shows 15672 listening solely on 10.100.130.x, not 0.0.0.0); firewalld public zone has no open port for 15672, only a rich rule permitting source 10.100.130.0/24; a peer node (node2) reached the API (HTTP 401, proving TCP+HTTP connectivity) confirming intra-cluster reachability while no broader exposure exists; rule set intact after restarts

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 910dc564... captured with service active; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; connection timed out mid-reboot; new boot_id ee6720dd... confirms restart; rabbitmq-server active again and quorum queue API shows state=running, all 3 members online post-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 67c52137... captured with service active; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; connection reset/timeout mid-reboot; new boot_id 4048d750... confirms restart; rabbitmq-server active again and cluster_status/queue API show full 3-node health with message intact

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 555221a1... captured with service active; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; connection dropped mid-reboot; new boot_id 7ec9eb65... confirms restart; rabbitmq-server active again and cluster_status/queue API show all 3 nodes running, quorum queue healthy with message intact, leader re-elected to node1

evidence.requirement: Data/queue durability verified across the full restart cycle
evidence.summary: A durable quorum queue with 1 persisted message was created before any restarts; after each of the three node restarts, the management API confirms state=running, messages=1, and all 3 members online, showing the message and quorum queue health survived every restart
